summary.headline: Sagility Q1 FY27 revenue rose 27.6% YoY to INR 19,635m; FY27 margin guidance held at 24-25% despite a 120 bps minimum-wage hit.
summary.overview: Revenue grew 27.6% YoY (15.2% in constant currency) to INR 19,635 million, with organic growth of 27.3% in INR and 14.9% in constant currency, helped by the CareSeed acquisition closed 11 June 2026. Sequentially, reported revenue fell because about $24.8 million of Q4 open-enrolment revenue did not recur, but steady-state organic revenue grew 5.1% QoQ in constant currency. Adjusted EBITDA rose 27.9% to INR 4,716 million at a 24.0% margin (down from 24.9% in Q4), and adjusted PAT rose 35.1% to INR 2,697 million at 13.7%. Management reiterated low double-digit FY27 organic constant-currency growth and the 24-25% margin range, with the wage impact absorbed via efficiencies and FX.

segments.name: CareSeed (quality/HEDIS, acquired)
segments.commentary: CY2025 revenue $5.1 million, 95% recurring, 31.4% EBITDA margin, 26 new mid/small-payer clients (each under $1m revenue); contributed INR 0.4 million in Q1 since 11 June 2026 close.

segments.name: BroadPath (acquired, Medicare sales/enrolment)
segments.commentary: Seasonal business; management said it lifted seasonal revenue share from about 3% (FY25) to about 6% (FY26). Standalone revenue not disclosed; the team said it would revert on numbers.

guidance_outlook: FY27 organic revenue growth guidance of low double-digit % in constant currency reiterated; management said it is 'very confident' of double-digit growth.
FY27 adjusted EBITDA margin guidance of 24-25% maintained; management said it should do better than the lower end if the wage impact comes in lower, with a narrower range expected at end of Q2.
Minimum wage impact estimated at about 120 bps on FY27 adjusted EBITDA; full-quarter impact from Q2 (Karnataka wage revision effective 23 May), roughly double the Q1 impact.
Seasonal OE/AEP revenue expected to recur in Q3 and Q4 FY27 at about 6% of revenue, similar to FY26; specifics expected by September, with more visibility at the October call.
Full mitigation of the minimum wage impact expected to take another 12-18 months.
FY27 debt to be fully repaid; ESOP pool of about 3% of equity under approval, grants not yet made.
capex_capacity: Fixed asset additions INR 745 million in Q1 FY27.
Expanding delivery in states outside Karnataka and Telangana (Tamil Nadu, Indore just started, Mumbai, Hyderabad exposure); less than 15-20% of employees are outside Karnataka and Telangana.
About 65-70% of headcount is in Bengaluru and Hyderabad, both affected by the wage revisions.
Pursuing M&A in clinical, provider-side and healthcare technology capabilities; RCM targets seen as high-valuation and not clearly capability-adding.
demand_pricing: Organic growth driven mainly by existing clients; management said growth is broad-based, with new FY26 clients starting to scale.
$35.3 million steady-state ACV signed in Q1 across 18 existing clients and 1 new logo; management said wins typically come from 15-20 clients a quarter.
No pricing increases taken; management said price movement is negative, with more pricing pressure than increases.
Top-4/5 client cohort growth soft because one client is moving onshore work offshore; management said such migrations are a recurring feature and are margin-accretive in general.
AI-led deflation expected at 100-150 bps historically, potentially rising to 200 bps over the near term; no quarterly tracking.
Payers: 70% of 50 decision-makers surveyed (Everest Group) say they adopted AI, but only 10% report measurable improvement.

qa_highlights.question: What share of minimum-wage staff is in Karnataka and Telangana, and is the 120 bps impact recurring and recoverable?
qa_highlights.answer: Less than 15-20% of employees are outside Karnataka and Telangana; the 120 bps impact includes cascading pay-parity effects; full mitigation expected in 12-18 months via efficiencies and expansion in other states.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the low double-digit guidance not higher given 5% QoQ underlying growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said QoQ growth should not be extrapolated; 14.9% organic growth in Q1 and confidence in double-digit growth for FY27 were reiterated, with narrower guidance at end-Q2.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a pricing lever in the 15% growth, and what is the split between new and old clients?
qa_highlights.answer: No pricing increases were taken; the client-level split of growth was not available and will be provided later.

qa_highlights.question: Why was margin guidance not raised despite 24% in Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Full-quarter minimum wage impact starts Q2 (about double the Q1 impact); FX gains and efficiencies offset; lower end is expected to be exceeded if the wage impact is lower.

qa_highlights.question: How much seasonal revenue was in FY25 vs FY26 and what drives FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Seasonal revenue was about $20 million in Q3+Q4 FY25 (about 3%) and about $50 million in FY26 (about 6%), boosted by BroadPath and a clinical seasonal client; FY27 expected at a similar percentage.

qa_highlights.question: Is M&A pipeline focused where?
qa_highlights.answer: Clinical, provider-side and healthcare technology capabilities; direct client-acquisition M&A is difficult given existing vendor relationships.

risks_watch: Minimum wage notification changes could alter the 120 bps FY27 impact; full-quarter impact from Q2.
Currency: management said FX gains (over 100 bps in Q1) helped hold margins; reversal would pressure the 24-25% range.
Client-level volume migration from onshore to offshore and AI-led deflation (100-200 bps) could weigh on revenue per client, as seen in the top 4/5 cohort.
Size and timing of seasonal OE/AEP revenue (about 6% of revenue) to be confirmed by September; management said deal timing is hard to predict.
BroadPath and CareSeed revenue not fully disclosed; organic growth definition relies on management's carve-outs.
Voluntary attrition 28.6% in Q1, still marginally above Q1 FY26.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the top line and balance sheet, with guidance reiterated; more cautious on margin and deal timing, deferring a narrower margin range to end-Q2. Several answers were vague on numbers (BroadPath revenue, client-level growth split, AI deflation), with management promising follow-ups.
key_quotes: Our Q1 performance reflects the continued relevance of our healthcare focused operating model, the depth of our client relationships, and the disciplined executions of our teams across geographies.
Sequentially, reported revenue declined versus Q4, reflecting the seasonal impact of open enrolment and AEP volumes that we support in Q3 and Q4.
we remain confident in our revenue outlook and reiterate our FY 2027 guidance of low double-digit organic growth in constant currency.
If the eventual outcome on minimum wages results in a lower impact, we could be at the upper end of that range or even higher.
